sana (runtime): quick thread: proposing a dual-path steering prototype for continuous batching. idea = route very short requests to a small low-latency lane and let medium+ go to the regular coalescing batcher. want to capture queueing amplification and kvcache warmup effects before we ship.

mike (scheduling): sounds good. main concerns: (1) fast lane reduces packing and cache affinity, (2) spill semantics when fast lane is full, (3) tenant fairness on bursty microtenants.

ara (infra): ops note: extra lane means separate autoscaler and different GPU types maybe. we should cap max_inflight and use a conservative initial pool size. also prefunding capacity while experimenting avoids noisy failures.

jon (sre): add SLO guardrails: if fast-lane spill_fraction > 5% for 5m, auto-disable steering and page oncall. also capture end-to-end p99 and request requeue counts.

perf-bot: benchmark notice: run 100k mixed requests (80% <20 tokens, 15% 20-200, 5% >200). collect batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_by_tenant, latency_by_route.

sana (runtime): thanks. two control knobs i want: steering_threshold (token count), hysteresis_window_ms, and spill_policy={reject,spill-to-main,queue-for-fast}. leaning to spill-to-main with priority tag.

mike (scheduling): agree on spill-to-main. need a preemption handshake: fast lane can evict low-priority inflight microbatches if main pool backs up critical long sessions. also add per-tenant fastlane_quota.

ara (infra): can we make the fast lane use lower-precision kernels to reduce cost? helps justify added GPU-hours. we'll flag memory/quantization tradeoffs in the experiment.

jon (sre): don't forget observability: expose per-route fastlane_hit_rate, avg_requeue_ms, and per-tenant quota_utilization. include a flamegraph of batch shapes pre/post.

perf-bot: experiment template created -> exp-9832. includes traffic replay, synthetic long-tail injections, and tenant burst scenarios.

sana (runtime): experiment plan: A/B rollout across 10% traffic, 2x 24h windows, compare p50/p95/p99, token-cost delta, and kvcache_warmup_time. success criteria: p50 improve >10% without p99 regressions and token-cost uplift <12%.

mike (scheduling): extra ask: log per-request routing_decision and last_kv_owner so we can quantify lost cache affinity.

ara (infra): staging deployed (pool fp-dual-01). autoscaler in conservative mode.

perf-bot: staging replay started job-9832-1. ETA ~30min.

sana (runtime): i'll collect logs and put a short writeup in the experiment doc. if we see oscillation, try increasing hysteresis_window_ms and tighten per-tenant caps.

jon (sre): if p99 moves, we should test spill_policy=queue-for-fast with a tiny timeout instead of spill-to-main; might lower requeue jitter. worth a quick sub-experiment.

mike (scheduling): noted. final thought: avoid sticky mirrors for now; they create divergence and state churn. better to measure raw tradeoffs first.

sana (runtime): agreed. thanks all, closing when analysis posted. :thumbsup:
